title: add-rag-adapter-starter-and-ts-mini-agent-example
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Adds a compact RAG adapter starter template plus a TypeScript mini-agent example and docs; intended as a low-friction onboarding path for engineers integrating retrieval and tool-calling into Redwood-powered apps.
description: Context: Customers and internal teams repeatedly asked for a minimal, production-minded example that wires retrieval, a small adapter layer, and a TypeScript agent runtime together without the overhead of a full orchestrator. Motivation: the existing RAG quickstarts focus on either heavy orchestrators or language bindings; this PR provides a focused starter that demonstrates (1) a retrieval adapter pattern for pluggable stores, (2) clear separation of prompt templates, retrieval scoring, and tool-calling hooks, and (3) a tiny TS agent runtime that can be dropped into Redwood API/Dedicated flows. What this PR adds: a) a new template at examples/rag-adapter-starter/ containing README, architecture diagram (SVG), and a minimal config (adapter-config.yaml) showing how to wire a vector store and a metadata filter; b) a TypeScript mini-agent in examples/rag-adapter-starter/ts-agent/ that implements a simple tool registry, a token-safe prompt renderer, and a streaming response adapter for Redwood API; c) docs site additions under docs/content/examples/rag-adapter-starter.md with step-by-step quickstart and suggested evals; d) CI smoke tests that run the TS example against a local mock retrieval endpoint and a small mocked Redwood API to validate end-to-end wiring. Quickstart (short): 1) git checkout feature branch && cd examples/rag-adapter-starter; 2) yarn install && yarn run start:mock to start the mocked retrieval + API; 3) yarn run demo --query "Explain zero-shot retrieval with simple examples". The README contains environment variables, optional KMS hints for private deployments, and notes on swapping adapter implementations. Commit summary: - initial scaffold and README (a49b3f) - TS mini-agent runtime + tool registry (c2e7d1) - docs and CI smoke tests (f9a1b4). High-level changed files: ["examples/rag-adapter-starter/README.md", "examples/rag-adapter-starter/ts-agent/index.ts", "examples/rag-adapter-starter/ts-agent/tool-registry.ts", "examples/rag-adapter-starter/adapter-config.yaml", "docs/content/examples/rag-adapter-starter.md", ".github/workflows/ci-smoke.yml", "examples/rag-adapter-starter/arch/diagram.svg"]. Testing & CI: CI added a lightweight smoke workflow (ci-smoke.yml) that spins up node-based mocks and runs the example integration tests. The workflow flaked once on macOS matrix due to a timing issue; fixed by adding a retry to the mock startup; final CI on merge shows all checks green. Security and privacy notes: the starter documents how to avoid including PII in embedded metadata, suggests configuring prefix-caching TTLs, and includes guidance for using customer KMS in Private deployments. Review conversation (high level): - Diego Martins (review): "Nice compact design. Can we avoid exposing raw API keys in the README examples?" - Author (Ava): "Good catch — swapped examples to use REDWOOD_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER and added a short KMS snippet." - Li Wei (review): "Tool-registry looks good; please add type guards for tool outputs to avoid unsafe JSON.parse." - Author: "Added runtime guards and unit tests for tool outputs (ts-agent/tool-registry.test.ts)." - Samir Khan (review, final): "Docs flow is clear; suggested a short troubleshooting section for common startup errors." - Author: "Added troubleshooting section and CI smoke test cases for the two startup errors noted." Merge outcome: Approved by all reviewers, CI passed on final run, merged via squash into main by Diego Martins on 2026-02-23. Back-compat: no public API changes; this is examples + docs only. Notes for maintainers: - keep the mock server lightweight; intended for local development only. - the adapter-config.yaml demonstrates three adapter hooks (fetch, filter, score); treat it as pattern guidance rather than a library API. Related work: references ENG-4823 (internal design doc), DOC-210 (example doc tracked in Docs backlog), SUP-76 (customer ask to simplify onboarding).
